title: Filling the communication and change management approaches
blurb: Place a piece of information under the right heading of the communication or change management approach, and judge whether an entry belongs there at all.
question: A project will use a collaboration platform with time-zone scheduling to update teams in Edinburgh and Pune. Under which heading of the communication management approach should this be recorded?

teach.h: Two people products, two different jobs
teach.body: The people element has two management products, both part of the PID and agreed in initiation. The communication management approach sets how the project communicates with, and hears from, its whole ecosystem. The change management approach sets the target organizational state and how the business moves there from the current state, through any interim states. Matching questions give you a piece of information and ask which heading it belongs under.

teach.h: The two approaches side by side

rows.label: Answers
values: Who hears what, how, how often; how we hear back
What changes for people, and how they get there

rows.label: Main headings
values: Stakeholder analysis; schedule and procedures; tools; resources
Characteristics of each state; enabling activities

rows.label: Lifecycle
values: Agreed in IP; reviewed at stage ends and closure
Agreed in IP; reviewed at stage ends and closure

teach.body: Stakeholder analysis: who is affected by the outcome or by the way the project is delivered, and who can influence its success or failure, with why. Communications schedule and procedures: for each stakeholder group, the purpose, frequency, channel or format and messaging. Supporting tools and techniques: for example communication platforms, analytics or automation tools. Resources: the people, time and money for the communication activities.

head: Heading
Example entry
rows: Union: represents permit officers whose jobs change; wants consulting
Union: monthly meeting; note to permit officers after each one
Email platform with open-rate analytics for resident updates
Half a communications officer's time; budget for printed letters
teach.caption: A platform is a TOOL; the people, time and money to run communications are RESOURCES.

teach.body: Characteristics of each state (current, any interim states, target), highlighting what changes: routines, practices, processes, culture, responsibilities, structure and capabilities. Enabling activities before, during and after the transition, such as consultation, trials, training and a help line. When deciding how much detail to include, consider the skills needed during and after transition, which areas are affected, key relationships, the evolving culture and how best to make the move.

items.label: Consult union and staff; train officers on exceptions
Private beta runs alongside paper; floorwalkers
Help line for residents; refresher training

teach.caption: Activities that help people make the move belong under enabling activities; descriptions of how things ARE belong under a state.

rows.label: How requests to change a baseline are approved
A specific risk with its probability and impact
Regular status to the project board

teach.note: A Practitioner item may ask whether an entry is appropriate. These are the classic misplacements.

items: 'Nine permit officers key in paper applications by hand; processing takes 11 days': characteristics of the CURRENT state.
'Officers handle the exceptions the online checks cannot resolve; a telephone route stays': characteristics of the TARGET state.
'Ward councillors fear older residents will be left behind': stakeholder analysis in the communication approach.

'Letters to every Old Town household two weeks before the private beta': schedule and procedures. 'How requests to change the agreed design are approved': not here at all; it is the issue management approach.

teach.text: Two classic slips. A virtual meeting or collaboration platform is a SUPPORTING TOOL, not a resource. And a description of today's routines and culture is the CURRENT state, even when it is written to explain why the project is needed.

items: Communication approach: stakeholder analysis; schedule and procedures; supporting tools and techniques; resources.
Change approach: characteristics of each state (current, interim, target); enabling activities before, during and after transition.
Platforms are tools; staff time and budget are resources.
Change control procedures, specific risks and benefit forecasts belong in other products.

summary: You can now place information under the right heading of the communication management approach or the change management approach, and spot entries that belong in another product such as the issue management approach, the risk register or the business case.

A.q: Calderbrook Borough Council's permit project will change the jobs of nine permit officers. Their trade union has asked to be consulted on the new ways of working and is respected by staff. Under which heading of the communication management approach should this information be recorded?
A.why: Stakeholder analysis identifies and analyses those affected by the outcome or the delivery of the project and those who can influence its success (3.4). The union, its interest and its influence belong there.

whyNot.1: The schedule would hold HOW and HOW OFTEN the project communicates with the union, not who they are and why they matter.
whyNot.2: Tools are platforms and techniques such as analytics; nothing here is a tool.
whyNot.3: Resources are the time and money for communication activities.

A.q: On Calderbrook's permit project, the project manager agrees a monthly meeting with the union branch secretary to discuss the new ways of working, with a short note sent to all permit officers after each meeting. Under which heading of the communication management approach should this be recorded?
A.why: The communications schedule and procedures set, for each stakeholder group, the purpose, frequency, channel or format and messaging (3.4). A monthly meeting plus a follow-up note is exactly that.

whyNot.0: The analysis records who the union is and why it matters; this entry says how and how often to communicate.
whyNot.2: A meeting and a note are channels in the schedule, not tools such as platforms or analytics.
whyNot.3: No staff time or budget is being allocated here.

A.q: Wenmoor Community Health is planning its single point of access. A note says: 'Referrals arrive through 14 routes, including email inboxes, phone lines and fax, and each locality's nurses decide which referrals they accept.' Under which heading of the change management approach should this be recorded?
A.why: The change management approach describes the characteristics of each state, highlighting what changes, such as processes and responsibilities (3.2.1). This describes how things work today.

whyNot.0: The target state is one referral route and a triage hub; this note describes the present.
whyNot.1: Enabling activities are actions that help people move, such as consultation or training; this is a description of a state.
whyNot.3: Activities during transition, such as trials, help people through the move; this is not an activity.

B.q: On Brennan Mutual's data centre exit, the team and its stakeholders are spread across Edinburgh and Pune. The project manager plans to use a collaboration platform with built-in translation and time-zone scheduling for team and stakeholder updates. Under which heading of the communication management approach should this be recorded?
B.why: Supporting tools and techniques include communication platforms and tools for analytics or automation (3.4). A collaboration platform is a tool, not a resource.

whyNot.0: Nothing here identifies or analyses a stakeholder.
whyNot.1: Resources are the people, time and money for communication activities; a platform is classed as a tool.
whyNot.3: The schedule sets purpose, frequency, channel and message per group; the platform supports that schedule.

B.q: On Carrowford's half marathon, the project manager secures two days a week of a council communications officer's time and £6,000 for printed letters to households on the route. Under which heading of the communication management approach should this be recorded?
B.why: The resources heading covers the resources for the communication activities (3.4): staff time and budget.

whyNot.0: The households are stakeholders, but this entry allocates time and money rather than analysing them.
whyNot.1: Tools are platforms and techniques; staff time and a print budget are resources.
whyNot.2: The letters themselves would appear in the schedule; the time and money to produce them are resources.

B.q: On Calderbrook's permit project, during the private beta, online and paper applications will run side by side, and the supplier's staff will sit with permit officers for the first two weeks to help them handle online exceptions. Under which heading of the change management approach should this be recorded?
B.why: Enabling activities before, during and after transition, such as trials and support, help people make the move (3.2.1). Parallel running with on-the-spot help happens during the transition.

whyNot.1: After-transition activities, such as a help line once the change is complete, follow the move; this support is while it is happening.
whyNot.2: The target state describes how things will be; this is an activity that helps people get there.
whyNot.3: Before-transition activities, such as consultation and training, come before the private beta starts.

C.q: At Wenmoor Community Health, the project manager's draft change management approach includes the procedure for raising, assessing and approving requests to change the baselined triage criteria. Is this an appropriate entry in the change management approach, and why?
options: Yes, because the triage criteria will change as the service moves to its target state
Yes, because the medical director must sign off any change to the triage criteria
No, because the approach is prepared by the business layer before the project starts
No, because control of changes to baselines belongs in the issue management approach
C.why: Change management is about people moving from current to target state (3.2.1); change control of baselined products is set out in the issue management approach under the issues practice.

whyNot.0: The criteria will change, but the procedure for approving baseline changes is change control, not change management.
whyNot.1: The sign-off rule is real, but it belongs in the change control procedure, which is not part of this approach.
whyNot.2: The change management approach is agreed in initiation as part of the PID.

C.q: At Fernhollow Foods, the stakeholder analysis in the communication management approach includes: 'Supermarket category buyer: decides listings and promotional space; strong influence on launch success; has been told all six recipes will launch.' Is this an appropriate entry, and why?
options: Yes, because stakeholder analysis covers those who can influence success or failure
Yes, because the buyer should be appointed as senior user for the new range
No, because external customers belong in the commercial management approach
No, because the buyer's expectations should be recorded in the risk register
C.why: Stakeholder analysis identifies and analyses those affected by the project and those who have the influence to affect its success or failure (3.4). The buyer's influence and expectations are exactly that.

whyNot.1: The buyer is an external customer, not the person accountable for user requirements and benefits inside Fernhollow.
whyNot.2: The commercial approach covers contracts and suppliers; analysing a stakeholder's influence belongs in stakeholder analysis.
whyNot.3: A related risk may also be registered, but that does not make the stakeholder analysis entry wrong.

C.q: On Brennan Mutual's data centre exit, the change management approach lists under 'Characteristics of the target state': 'Operations staff work as cloud operations engineers on a 24-hour on-call rota, monitoring the cloud platform rather than physical hardware.' Is this an appropriate entry, and why?
options: Yes, because the target state is where the business case's benefits are listed
Yes, because state characteristics show what changes in routines and responsibilities
No, because staffing details belong in the project management team structure
No, because retraining staff is an enabling activity rather than a state
C.why: The change management approach sets out the characteristics of each state, highlighting what changes, such as routines, responsibilities and capabilities (3.2.1). This describes how operations will work after the move.

whyNot.0: Benefits are forecast in the business case; the target state describes how the organization will operate.
whyNot.2: The PMT structure covers project roles; this entry describes business-as-usual roles after the change.
whyNot.3: Retraining would be an enabling activity, but this entry describes the end state, not the training.

reteach.title: Is it a description, an activity, or a way of talking?
reteach.question: Read the piece of information and ask: does it describe how things are, help people move, or say who we talk to and how?

blocks.body: A DESCRIPTION of how people work (today, in between, or after) goes under a state in the change management approach. An ACTIVITY that helps people move, such as consultation, trials, training or a help line, goes under enabling activities before, during or after. Anything about WHO the project talks to and HOW goes in the communication management approach: the analysis, the schedule, the tools or the resources.

head: Information
Heading
rows: 'Today staff key in forms by hand'

blocks.text: If the information is about approving changes to agreed products, it belongs in neither people product: it is the issue management approach.

explain.body: Before choosing a heading, check the information belongs in this product at all. Specific risks with probability and impact go in the risk register; change control goes in the issue management approach.

test.q: On Carrowford's half marathon, the draft communication management approach includes: 'Risk: heavy rain reduces spectator numbers. Probability medium, impact high. Owner: events manager.' Is this an appropriate entry in the communication management approach, and why?
options: Yes, because spectators are stakeholders whose numbers affect the event
Yes, because the approach should describe how risks will be communicated
No, because a specific risk with its assessment belongs in the risk register
No, because weather is outside the project's control and should not be recorded
test.why: Specific risks, with their probability, impact and owner, are recorded in the risk register (risk practice); the communication approach covers stakeholders, schedules, tools and resources (3.4).

whyNot.0: Spectators are stakeholders, but this entry is a risk assessment, not a stakeholder analysis.
whyNot.1: Describing how risk information is communicated could fit, but this entry records a specific risk and its assessment.
whyNot.3: Risks outside the project's control are still recorded and managed; they just do not belong here.

explain.body: For each stakeholder group the schedule sets the purpose, frequency, channel or format and messaging. If an entry says how, how often or what to say to a group, it belongs here.

test.q: At Wenmoor Community Health, an entry reads: 'Patients' forum: purpose, co-design a direct referral route for carers; channel, forum meeting; frequency, every two months; message, design options and decisions so far.' Under which heading of the communication management approach should this be recorded?
test.why: The communications schedule and procedures set purpose, frequency, channels or format and messaging for each stakeholder group (3.4).

whyNot.0: The analysis records who the forum is and why it matters; this entry sets how and when to communicate.
whyNot.2: No platform or technique is named; a forum meeting is a channel in the schedule.
whyNot.3: No staff time or budget is allocated in this entry.

explain.body: State characteristics describe how the organization works in the current, interim or target state, highlighting what changes: routines, practices, processes, culture, responsibilities, structure and capabilities.

test.q: On Calderbrook's permit project, a note reads: 'After go-live, a smaller team of permit officers will handle the applications that the automatic checks cannot resolve, and a telephone assisted route will remain for residents who cannot apply online.' Under which heading of the change management approach should this be recorded?
test.why: The note describes how the service will work once the change is complete, so it is a characteristic of the target state (3.2.1).

whyNot.0: The current state is the paper process keyed by hand; this describes the future.
whyNot.1: Activities after transition, such as a help line, help people settle in; this describes how the service will be set up.
whyNot.2: Activities during transition, such as parallel running, are temporary; this is the lasting arrangement.

explain.body: Enabling activities help people through the move: before it (consultation, training), during it (trials, side-by-side running), and after it (help line, refresher support).

test.q: At Fernhollow Foods, the line supplier's engineer will staff a help line for the night shift operators for the first month after the new tray-sealing line goes into normal production. Under which heading of the change management approach should this be recorded?
test.why: Enabling activities after transition, such as a help line, support people once the change has been made (3.2.1).

whyNot.0: Before-transition activities, such as training, come before the line goes live.
whyNot.2: The target state describes how the line will be run; the help line is a temporary activity supporting people.
whyNot.3: An interim state is a stage between current and target; the help line is an activity, not a state.
